problem.requested_solution: Deploy an AI agent that automatically detects, corrects, and resubmits rejected shipment notices.
symptoms: Reject log (E-01) shows 3 rejected shipment notices: N-1 and N-2 rejected for LOC_UNKNOWN, N-3 rejected for EVENT_ORDER.
Stakeholder claims about the root cause conflict: CL-01 (correctable content errors) vs CL-02 (flaky carrier, resubmit blindly), tracked as open conflicts C-1 and C-2.
problem.root_problem: Shipment notices sent from Shipper (ORG-A) to Carrier (ORG-B) via H-1, though marked semantically VALID by the shipper's own validation, are rejected because the carrier applies different acceptance criteria: 2 notices (N-1, N-2) fail because the carrier does not recognize a submitted location code/value (LOC_UNKNOWN), and 1 notice (N-3) fails because events are processed out of the carrier's expected order (EVENT_ORDER), per the authoritative reject log (E-01).

framing_assertion.rationale: The initial request to 'auto-fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them' presupposes that rejects stem from fixable data/content errors in the notices themselves, rather than from a deeper business or communication mismatch.

hypotheses.statement: Shipment notices are rejected because of content/data errors on the Shipper (ORG-A) side that an AI agent could detect, correct, and resubmit.
hypotheses.rationale: This is SH-REQ's stated framing and the entire proposed solution (auto-fix agent) only makes sense if this is true; if false, building an auto-fix/resubmit agent would be the wrong intervention.

hypotheses.statement: Rejects are legitimate carrier business decisions (e.g., contract, capacity, or policy mismatches) rather than data errors, so resubmitting corrected notices would not change the outcome.
hypotheses.rationale: The reject-log tool is explicitly described as capturing 'carrier business rejects', suggesting rejections may be rule-based business decisions rather than malformed-data issues, which would make auto-fix-and-resubmit ineffective or even harmful.

hypotheses.statement: The shipper's notion of a valid notice (H-1 marked semantic_validity VALID) differs from the carrier's actual acceptance criteria, so technically 'valid' notices still get rejected downstream.
hypotheses.rationale: H-1 shows delivery_status HEALTHY and semantic_validity VALID at the handoff, yet rejects still occur at ORG-B, implying the gap is between two different validation standards rather than a single fixable defect.

key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): shipment notices sent ORG-A→ORG-B via handoff H-1 are marked semantically VALID by the shipper's own validation, yet the carrier rejects some of them under different acceptance criteria (E-01, A-SHIPPER-SIDE-VALIDITY).
The authoritative reject log (E-01, data asset DA-REJ) shows 3 reject records: N-1 and N-2 rejected for LOC_UNKNOWN, N-3 rejected for EVENT_ORDER (F-01).

The requester (SH-REQ) initially asked for an AI agent to auto-fix and resubmit rejects (CL-01), but later gave a conflicting, non-authoritative claim that the carrier is 'flaky' and everything should just be resubmitted (CL-02/E-02); this conflict is tracked as open C-1/C-2 and the flaky-carrier narrative is unsubstantiated (H-FLAKY-CARRIER-UNSUBSTANTIATE, supported by E-02 but contradicted by nothing in E-01).

Supported hypotheses explaining the rejects are a semantic criteria gap between shipper and carrier (H-SEMANTIC-CRITERIA-GAP) and an event-sequencing issue for N-3 (H-EVENT-SEQUENCING-ISSUE); the 'legitimate business decision' hypothesis was REJECTED (H-BUSINESS-REJECT-MISMATCH).
The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring the critical unknown about whether LOC_UNKNOWN is deterministically fixable to VOB-U-LOC-UNKNOWN-FIX-FEASIBILITY (recent_events seq 51).

What was actually released (SD-1 release_scope) is limited to analyzing reject reasons (DA-REJ) and flagging reasons without a verified fix mapping for human review by interface owner SH-INT; both corresponding work items (W-WI-ANALYZE-REJECTS, W-WI-FLAG-UNMAPPED) are DONE.

Automated correction and resubmission of LOC_UNKNOWN or EVENT_ORDER notices (part of the original intended_scope) was NOT released, because the open verification obligations (VOB-U-LOC-UNKNOWN-FIX-FEASIBILITY, VOB-R-2, VOB-R-3) block exactly that correction/sequencing scope, which falls outside what was actually shipped.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no HOLD items: the delivered analysis-and-flagging scope does not depend on the still-open feasibility and completeness unknowns, so it can go out while correction logic remains deferred.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS; items it could not resolve were deferred as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than closed out.

Three verification obligations remain OPEN and are required BEFORE_RELEASE in principle, but their blocking scope (correcting LOC_UNKNOWN, resolving EVENT_ORDER sequencing) lies outside what was actually released, so they did not stop this narrower release.
The root-cause diagnosis rests on only 3 observed reject records (N-1, N-2, N-3 in E-01); the true distribution of reject reasons across the full notice volume is not established.
Completeness of the carrier reject log itself is UNKNOWN (U-REJECT-LOG-COMPLETENESS); with only 3 sample records observed, the real reason-code mix could differ from what's seen so far.

No verified deterministic fix exists yet for LOC_UNKNOWN (VOB-U-LOC-UNKNOWN-FIX-FEASIBILITY, still OPEN) or for EVENT_ORDER (U-EVENT-ORDER-FIX-MECHANISM, still OPEN); as a result, automated correction and resubmission were excluded from this release entirely.

Two structural remedies that would remove the root cause -- a data contract so ORG-A can validate location codes against ORG-B's reference list (SR-R1), and reordering shipment-notice events upstream to match carrier expectations (SR-R2) -- were identified but are not feasible within the current scope/time and were not implemented; the agent also lacks write authority to implement them.

A requester-side conflict about root cause remains unresolved: the original claim that rejects are correctable content errors (CL-01) and a later claim that the carrier is simply flaky and should be blindly resubmitted (CL-02) are tracked as open conflicts C-1 and C-2, and the flaky-carrier claim is not corroborated by the authoritative reject log.
output.summary: The defined problem (PD-1) is that shipment notices from the Shipper (ORG-A) to the Carrier (ORG-B) via handoff H-1, though marked semantically VALID by the shipper's own validation, are rejected by the carrier for different reasons: the authoritative reject log (E-01) shows N-1 and N-2 rejected for LOC_UNKNOWN and N-3 for EVENT_ORDER (F-01). This was established by analyzing the carrier reject log and testing it against two conflicting stakeholder claims from SH-REQ -- that rejects are correctable content errors (CL-01, the original request) versus that the carrier is just 'flaky' and everything should be blindly resubmitted (CL-02/E-02) -- with the semantic-criteria-gap and event-sequencing hypotheses coming out SUPPORTED and the business-rejection hypothesis REJECTED. The DEFINE gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring the hardest unknowns (notably whether LOC_UNKNOWN is deterministically fixable) as verification obligations (VOBs). What was actually released is a narrow scope: analyzing the reject-reason distribution from the reject log, and flagging any reject reason lacking a verified fix mapping for routing to the carrier-side interface owner (SH-INT) for human review; both corresponding work items are DONE. Automated correction and resubmission of rejected notices -- the original requested solution -- was deliberately excluded, because the open verification obligations block exactly that scope and no verified fix mechanism exists yet for either reject reason. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with nothing on HOLD: the released scope does not depend on the still-open unknowns, so it can ship now while the harder, structural fixes remain for later work.
